newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Antwerp port strike extended to Tuesday night.
newsitem.headline: Antwerp port strike extended to Tuesday night.

text.p: A 24-hour strike that began at 0700 GMT on Monday at the Belgian port of Antwerp has been extended to 1900 GMT on Tuesday, the Belga news agency reported.
The strike, at the second-biggest port in Europe after Rotterdam in the Netherlands, brought all movement to a halt, port authorities said.
"All the locks are blocked by strikers. The entire port is blocked," a port authority spokesman told Reuters.
He said some pilot services were working and a few bridges were open, but no traffic was possible because of the closure of the locks.
Port authority workers are striking in protest over a planned change in their status from public sector workers to private sector workers.
Dutch meals and feeds traders said the stoppage had little impact on the animal feed market as Antwerp was not the main gateway into Europe for the trade.
